submissions.title: Memphis 18-month data center moratorium fails to pass
submissions.excerpt: Memphis 18-month data center moratorium fails to pass
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Memphis City Council's proposed moratorium on new data center development (originally drafted as 12 months, brought to this vote as 18 months) failed on a 6-6 tie vote on Oct 20, 2026 (Councilwoman Yolanda Cooper-Sutton was absent; a motion to delay the vote also failed). This followed a chaotic Oct 6 session (7-5 vote to postpone) marked by protests and a physical altercation. Reporting conflicts on what happened immediately after the tie: one outlet (World Today Journal, lower reliability, unverified elsewhere) says the council passed a substitute 135-day ban instead; others describe only a separate council-ordered 90-day administrative review of data center regulations led by Mayor Paul Young. Recommend the reviewer confirm the actual outcome via the council's own minutes or the Daily Memphian/Commercial Appeal before recording any 'restriction in effect' status. Directly relevant to this tracker's two Memphis-area projects, xAI Colossus 2 (Memphis, TN) and xAI MACROHARDRR (Southaven, MS) — both cited by name repeatedly in the underlying debate.

submissions.title: San Francisco, Oakland pass 45-day moratoriums on new data centers
submissions.excerpt: San Francisco, Oakland pass 45-day moratoriums on new data centers
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors unanimously passed a 45-day moratorium halting new data center approvals and expansions citywide (vote Oct 6-7, 2026, sponsored by Supervisor Shamann Walton); Mayor Daniel Lurie signed it into law Oct 16, 2026 (would have taken effect without his signature). It can be extended up to roughly 22 months pending a Planning Department environmental-impact study due by a November 2026 hearing; a permanent ordinance could follow. Oakland reportedly passed a similar 45-day measure the same week per this source — not independently confirmed here, worth a separate look on a future run. No project in this tracker is currently sited in San Francisco or Oakland; flagging as part of a broader October 2026 wave of municipal data-center restrictions alongside Memphis TN and Lexington KY (see companion submissions).

submissions.title: TeraWulf Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
submissions.excerpt: CB3 was fully delivered and generating lease revenue in early July, bringing total revenue-generating critical IT capacity at the campus to 102 megawatts.
submissions.note: Tracked project: TeraWulf Lake Mariner (slug terawulf-lake-mariner-fluidstack-anthropic), currently carries estimatedMw=360 with no confirmedMw. Update: following completion of building CB-3 in early July 2026, revenue-generating (i.e. leased and billable) critical IT capacity at the campus reached 102 MW, up from 81 MW as of June 30, 2026 — this is a confirmed, contracted-and-energized figure, distinct from the ~360 MW estimated full-build total. The CB-3 delivery also triggered $600M of Google's credit support for Fluidstack's lease obligations to become effective. An additional 336 MW (CB-4, CB-5) remains under construction, phased delivery through early 2027. Caveat: the quoted sentence is reconstructed from a secondary Q2 2026 earnings-call transcript (Benzinga), not read directly off the linked SEC filing — WebFetch/curl had no outbound network access to any external host this run (only WebSearch worked), so the exact wording could not be verified character-for-character against the primary filing. Please confirm against the filing or investors.terawulf.com before promoting to CONFIRMED.

claims.methodology: TeraWulf management stated total revenue-generating critical IT capacity at Lake Mariner reached 102 MW after CB-3 delivery in early July 2026, per Q2 2026 earnings release/call; wording reconstructed from a secondary transcript, not independently verified against primary filing text in this run.

submissions.title: IREN Delivers Horizon 1 to Microsoft and Achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud Status on GB300 NVL72
submissions.excerpt: Horizon 1, the first of four 50MW (IT load) direct-to-chip liquid-cooled deployments, has been delivered to and accepted by Microsoft.
submissions.note: Tracked project: IREN Childress Horizon (slug iren-childress-horizon-for-microsoft), currently estimatedMw=750 with analyst notes stating 'Horizon 1 handover targeted Q3 2026.' Update: the handover occurred and was accepted by Microsoft on Aug 13, 2026 — confirmed delivery of the first of four 50MW IT-load tranches under the $9.7B, 5-year Childress cloud-services contract (announced Nov 2025); IREN also reported NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on its GB300 NVL72 deployment there. Horizons 2-4 (remaining 150MW IT) were still targeted for delivery 'later this year' as of the release. Caveat: as with the TeraWulf submission above, the quote is reconstructed from secondary coverage (DatacenterDynamics, The Block, GreenStockNews, TaiwanNews) describing IREN's GlobeNewswire release — WebFetch/curl could not reach the primary release or this SEC filing directly this run to confirm exact wording. Please verify against the linked 8-K or iren.gcs-web.com before treating the quote as literal.

claims.methodology: IREN announced Horizon 1, the first of four 50MW IT-load tranches at its Childress, TX campus, was delivered to and accepted by Microsoft on Aug 13, 2026; figure corroborated across multiple outlets but not independently verified against primary-source text in this run.

submissions.title: Lexington council extends data center ban
submissions.excerpt: Lexington council extends data center ban
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Council (KY) voted unanimously around Oct 6-7, 2026 to extend its existing data center development moratorium — otherwise set to expire Oct 31, 2026 — through October 2027, and advanced a zoning text amendment (ZOTA) restricting large data centers. Figures conflict across sources and across the planning-commission-vs-council stages of this process: some outlets describe a ban on facilities over 50,000 sq ft, while earlier (July 2026) planning-commission coverage cites a 40,000 sq ft threshold; both stages describe a 25 MW energy-use cap and (per the council version) a 30 dB noise limit, plus a proposal to create a new 'exclusive use zone' classification for smaller data centers. Deliberately leaving the size-threshold figure blank rather than guessing between 40,000 and 50,000 sq ft — recommend the reviewer check the council's adopted ordinance text directly. No project in this tracker is sited in Lexington, KY.

submissions.title: NextEra, Brookfield to Build $100 Billion Data Center Campus
submissions.excerpt: NextEra, Brookfield to Build $100 Billion Data Center Campus
submissions.suggestedProjectName: NextEra–Brookfield Paducah AI Data Center Campus
submissions.note: New project, not found in the current data/projects.csv snapshot. Announced Jul 29, 2026 (older than this run's ideal ~24-72h recency window, but never captured, so flagging now): a consortium led by NextEra Energy and Brookfield plans a >$100B AI data center campus at the US DOE's former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant (a closed uranium-enrichment site), McCracken County, Kentucky, targeting completion by 2032. NextEra would build ~2 GW of co-located natural-gas generation plus 2.6 GW of battery storage; Brookfield would own/operate the data center campus itself. Power-vs-compute basis is genuinely unresolved in reporting and should NOT be collapsed into one figure: most outlets (Bloomberg Law, The Star, IREI) describe '1.8 GW' as the Brookfield-operated campus capacity, a DealStreetAsia/Reuters version instead describes 1.8 GW as power that could be supplied to the grid, and a separate outlet cites 'more than 1.2 GW of computing capacity.' Leaving MW blank pending the definitive agreement, which multiple sources note is still subject to negotiation. Claimed ~8,000 construction jobs, ~600 permanent jobs. NextEra CEO John Ketchum quoted: "The data center will bring its own power, pay for its own power infrastructure and create good-paying jobs for local workers."

claims.methodology: NextEra and Brookfield jointly announced a planned investment of more than $100B in the Kentucky Paducah data center campus (Jul 29, 2026 company announcement), as reported by multiple outlets (Bloomberg Law, Reuters/DealStreetAsia, The Star); the project remains subject to negotiation of definitive documentation.
